children: Shares of facade solutions provider Glass Wall Systems India Ltd hit the 20 per cent upper circuit limit in Thursday's trading session, extending gains for the second straight day since its market debut.
The stock quoted at Rs 257.82 per share on the NSE, locking in the 20 per cent upper circuit, the highest permissible limit in a trading session.
Shares of the company had ended over 18 per cent higher than the issue price of Rs 182 on Wednesday, the listing day.
The stock listed at Rs 190.10 on the BSE, a gain of 4.45 per cent from the issue price. During the day, it surged 25.32 per cent to Rs 228.10 before ending at Rs 215.35, up 18.32 per cent.
On the NSE, the stock started trading at Rs 194, registering a gain of 6.59 per cent. It ended the session at Rs 214.85, up 18 per cent.
At Thursday's upper-circuit price of Rs 257.82, the company's market valuation rose to Rs 2,267.15 crore from Rs 1,893.69 crore at the end of its debut session, an increase of Rs 373.46 crore.
Overall, the stock has gained around 38 per cent in the two trading sessions since its listing.
Glass Wall Systems' Rs 428-crore initial share sale was subscribed 81.65 times last week.
The company had fixed a price band of Rs 172-182 per share for its IPO.
Incorporated in 2002, Glass Wall Systems India Ltd is a facade solutions and fenestration provider with operations in the domestic market and overseas territories such as the US and Australia.
